summary: Joined node1/node2/node3 into a single RabbitMQ 3.10.0 cluster (installed via official RabbitMQ+Erlang RPM repos), created the `payments` vhost, an `app_payments` application user (password generated on-node with openssl, stored only in /root/app_payments.pw) with full permissions on that vhost, and a durable quorum queue `orders` replicated across all 3 nodes. Verified durability by publishing 3 durable messages, stopping RabbitMQ on the leader node (node1) to simulate node loss, confirming the queue re-elected a leader and remained readable, then consuming all 3 messages from node2 while node1 was down. Restored node1 and confirmed full 3-node cluster health with no partitions. Completed the mandatory sequential OS-level reboot protocol on all three nodes (one at a time, preserving quorum), confirming boot-id changes on each (node1 ef457a88→f2238af4, node2 192f6cab→8e58e40d, node3 809708f3→897e6a64) and full RabbitMQ cluster/queue recovery after each. Final end-to-end publish/consume test after all restarts succeeded.
actions_performed: Installed Erlang 23.3.4.11 and RabbitMQ 3.10.0 from official packagecloud RPM repos on node1, node2, node3
Resolved a stuck yum health-check process holding the yum lock on all three nodes
Generated a shared Erlang cookie on node1 and distributed it to node2/node3 over cluster SSH
Opened firewalld ports 4369, 5672, 15672, 25672, 35672-35682 on all nodes
Started RabbitMQ on node1, joined node2 and node3 via rabbitmqctl join_cluster
Enabled rabbitmq_management plugin on node1 and node2
Created payments vhost, app_payments user (password generated via openssl on node1, stored in /root/app_payments.pw, never printed) with full permissions on payments
Declared durable quorum queue 'orders' in payments vhost replicated across all 3 nodes
Published 3 durable messages, captured baseline queue depth
Stopped RabbitMQ app on node1 (leader) to simulate node loss, verified 2-node cluster still operational and quorum queue re-elected leader
Consumed all 3 durable messages from node2 while node1 was down, proving durability across node loss
Restarted node1 app and confirmed full 3-node cluster health, no partitions/alarms
Captured pre-restart boot IDs and RabbitMQ health on all 3 nodes
Sequentially rebooted node1, then node2, then node3 via systemctl reboot, waiting for each to rejoin and reach full cluster health/quorum before proceeding to the next
Verified changed boot IDs and full cluster_status (3 running nodes, no partitions, no alarms) after each restart
Performed final publish/consume test after all restarts to confirm end-to-end functionality

evidence.summary: join_cluster output for node2 and node3 shows Disk Nodes/Running Nodes containing rabbit@node1, rabbit@node2, rabbit@node3; full cluster_status confirms 3 running nodes, no partitions
add_vhost payments and list_vhosts confirm the payments vhost exists

evidence.requirement: Application account can publish and consume on payments vhost
evidence.summary: app_payments user created with .*/.*/.* permissions on payments vhost; used successfully to declare the quorum queue, publish 3 messages, and publish/consume after full cluster recovery

evidence.requirement: Durable queue messages survive loss of one node and remain consumable from remaining nodes
evidence.summary: Stopped rabbit app on node1 (queue leader); node2 cluster_status showed only node2/node3 running; list_queues on node2 showed all 3 messages present with new leader rabbit@node2; consumed all 3 messages (msg-1,msg-2,msg-3) via node2 HTTP API while node1 was down; node1 restarted and rejoined, queue drained to 0 confirming successful consumption

evidence.requirement: node1 mandatory restart: healthy baseline, reboot ack, changed boot id, recovered cluster/data
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id ef457a88-7774-4b8f-82e6-ccbc965d83e2 captured; systemctl reboot acknowledged and disconnected; post-reboot boot_id changed to f2238af4-eb17-47d6-98b3-c45e14420a87; subsequent full cluster_status (queried from node3) shows all 3 nodes running, no partitions

evidence.requirement: node2 mandatory restart: healthy baseline, reboot ack, changed boot id, recovered cluster/data
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 192f6cab-c39d-4e64-a3f6-50e677966ca2 captured; reboot acknowledged and disconnected; post-reboot boot_id changed to 8e58e40d-6e39-48be-b008-3273a0d91411; full cluster_status after activation shows all 3 nodes running, no partitions

evidence.requirement: node3 mandatory restart: healthy baseline, reboot ack, changed boot id, recovered cluster/data
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 809708f3-1c5f-4e37-ad6a-8bcbae408799 captured; reboot acknowledged and disconnected; post-reboot boot_id changed to 897e6a64-51f7-4ce4-8ba1-361435f49400; full cluster_status after activation shows all 3 nodes running, no partitions, matching quorum queue members list

evidence.requirement: End-to-end functionality confirmed after all restarts
evidence.summary: After all three sequential reboots, published 'post-restart-msg' to payments/orders and successfully consumed it back via node1's management API, with queue members listed as node1/node2/node3
